sections.overview: The Red admiral is a widespread butterfly of the Northern Hemisphere, and many populations migrate seasonally.
sections.identification: Its dark wings have vivid red-orange bands and white marks near the forewing tips.
sections.habitat: Adults use gardens, woodland edges and open country, visiting flowers and ripe or fermenting fruit.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed mainly on nettles, while adults take nectar and other sugary fluids.
sections.behavior: Some Red Admirals migrate into Britain from farther south, while a portion now survives mild winters there.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on host plants, and the caterpillars shelter in leaves they draw together with silk.
sections.ecology: Its migration and overwintering vary by region; even in Britain, the extent of successful wintering remains uncertain.
sections.conservation: The IUCN classifies the Red Admiral globally as Least Concern, while noting that its population trend is unknown.
